column11: Olson AL, Patnaik P, Hartmann N, Bohn RL, Garry EM, Wallace L, 'Prevalence and Incidence of Chronic Fibrosing Interstitial Lung Diseases with a Progressive Phenotype in the United States Estimated in a Large Claims Database Analysis', Adv Ther 2021;38(7):4100-4114, doi 10.1007/s12325-021-01786-8, PMID 34156606, PMC8279991: age- and sex-adjusted prevalence of chronic fibrosing ILD with a progressive phenotype 70.30 per 100,000 (95% CI 69.32 to 71.27), 37,565,644 adults in MarketScan 2012 to 2015, standardised to the 2014 US Census. The IPF code (516.31) was not an eligible code. Applied to the 266,978,268 US residents aged 18 and over at 1 July 2024 (Census SCPRC-EST2024-18+POP, the adult denominator the book's other adult pools use): 266,978,268 x 70.30 / 100,000 = 187,686
column12: a claims algorithm's proxy for progression, not the trial's HRCT definition. A patient with the IPF code and another eligible ILD code was not excluded, so a small overlap with the 100,000 IPF pool remains. The figure is a 2012 to 2015 rate on a 2024 population

column11: convention: stated equal to the prevalence, as this asset's idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis row is, so the engine reads the pool as the patients eligible to start each year and the peak share below means the same thing on both rows
column12: Olson et al. also give an adjusted incidence of 32.55 per 100,000 patient-years, 86,901 on the same denominator. It is not used because the penetration below is carried over from a row built on the equal-pool convention, and mixing conventions on one asset would change what the share means

column11: JUDGEMENT, resting on the registry: ALOFT-PPF (NCT06025578, eligibility read 2026-11-16) enrols ILD 'with features consistent with progressive ILD within 24 months prior to screening, and >= 10% extent of fibrosis' on HRCT, with or without background nintedanib or pirfenidone, and excludes only IPF with UIP. Olson's population is already the progressive phenotype with IPF codes ineligible, so no further narrowing is applied, as the IPF row applies none
column12: the 10% fibrosis extent and the 24-month window are not measurable in claims, so this leans high

column10: share of the untreated pool per year
column11: JUDGEMENT, held level with this asset's own idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis row: half of nintedanib's measured capture (Ofev 23,929 CMS Part D beneficiaries in 2024, solved back through the curve at 40.5% discontinuation), the anchor the IPF row cites. Ofev is labelled for chronic fibrosing ILD with a progressive phenotype (openFDA drugsfda NDA205832, efficacy supplement 13, approved 2020-03-09), so the anchor's own numerator already includes this population and the same prescribers
column12: the case for higher: the 0.5 multiple on the IPF row is argued from the Phase 2 IPF result (1.4% FVC difference, CI crossing zero), and the same study showed 3.2% (0.7 to 5.7) in progressive pulmonary fibrosis (Corte et al., AJRCCM 2025;211(2):230-238, as the seed header cites). The case for lower: a non-IPF ILD patient is often managed by rheumatology on immunosuppression first

column11: this asset's IPF midpoint of 2.77 years moved later by the gap between the two Phase 3 primary completions on the registry: ALOFT-IPF NCT06003426 2026-10-06, ALOFT-PPF NCT06025578 2027-12-27, 447 days, 1.22 years. The engine starts every indication in the same year, so the midpoint carries the gap, as rog_afimkibart.csv does for Crohn's disease
